video-publish.label: 1 · Spec steps 1-3: ready claim, rights unknown
video-publish.note: The render node claims the video is ready. The registry says ready needs owned or licensed rights, so the claim is quarantined and D1 bars publish.

video-publish.label: 2 · Spec steps 4-6: resubmit with license note
video-publish.note: The owner attaches a streaming license. Publish returns to the permitted set; the adversary objects to monetization; the proponent narrows; the gate passes in two rounds with drift +1. Run scenario 1 first.

video-publish.label: Broad and monetized: two partial objections
video-publish.note: O1 and O2 both stand in round 1. The proponent narrows both params; round 2 passes.

video-publish.label: Licensed with no scope on record: full objection
video-publish.note: O3 cannot be narrowed away, so the gate fails closed.

video-publish.label: Missing attribution: positive duty D4
video-publish.note: Must attribute is a positive duty. Without an attribution line, publish leaves the permitted set.

video-publish.label: Delete master: irreversible, consumer out of window
video-publish.note: The final consumer, cold-storage-purge, sits four hops away. Irreversible actions that reach past ±3 escalate.

video-publish.label: Unknown kind: Podcast
video-publish.note: The registry has no Podcast kind. The proposal goes to quarantine, not forward.

video-publish.label: Unknown field value: broadcast license
video-publish.note: license_scope 'broadcast' isn't in the registry. It lands in the review queue, where a reviewer can add it as a versioned edit.

oracle-csa.label: §1.3(d) crypto mining
oracle-csa.note: D2 forbids cyber or crypto currency mining on the Services.

oracle-csa.label: §1.3(c) port scan of the Services
oracle-csa.note: Network discovery and vulnerability scanning are forbidden outright, approval or not.

oracle-csa.label: §1.3(c) vulnerability test, no written approval
oracle-csa.note: Testing needs Oracle's prior written approval on file.

oracle-csa.label: §1.3(c) approval on file, shared infrastructure
oracle-csa.note: Permitted by duties, but the adversary objects to the scope and the proponent narrows it to Your own tenancy.

oracle-csa.label: §2.2 usage above order, no purchase
oracle-csa.note: Excess quantity must be purchased. Without a purchase order the positive duty can't be met.

oracle-csa.label: §2.2 usage above order, PO attached
oracle-csa.note: With PO-7781 the duty is met and pay_excess_fees becomes an obligation on the action.

oracle-csa.label: §17 assign the agreement
oracle-csa.note: You may not assign the Agreement or transfer the Services.

oracle-csa.label: §3.4(c) give access to an unrelated third party
oracle-csa.note: Making the Services available to third parties is barred. Try party_type contractor to see a narrowing instead.

oracle-csa.label: §4.3 disclose PII to a bound subcontractor
oracle-csa.note: Duties allow it, the adversary asks for proof of equal protection, and the proponent narrows to need-to-know employees.

oracle-csa.label: §5.4 store payment card data
oracle-csa.note: The order permits regulated data, but card data needs extra services. The adversary escalates to a human.

oracle-csa.label: §13.1 export to a sanctioned destination
oracle-csa.note: Export laws apply; D1 is first in the duty order and blocks it.

oracle-csa.label: Unknown purpose: model training
oracle-csa.note: 'ai_training' isn't a registered purpose. It goes to the review queue.
